translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus, who belong to Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavens through Christ.
Just as he chose us in him before the creation of the world, so that we should be holy and blameless before him in love.
He predestined us beforehand for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, which he freely gave us through the Beloved,
in whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our sins, according to the riches of his grace,
which he lavished on us in all wisdom and understanding.
He made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure, which he determined beforehand in him
for the ordering of the fullness of the times: to bring all things together under Christ as head, whatever is in the heavens and on earth;
in him, in whom we too were appointed and predestined by the will of God, who made all things according to the counsel of his will,
so that we, who first hoped in Christ, should be to the praise of his glory.
In him you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation; in it you believed and were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the redemption of our possession, to the praise of his glory.
For this reason I too, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus Christ and of the love that you have toward all the saints,
do not cease giving thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him,
and may enlighten the eyes of your heart, so that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what are the riches of the glory of his inheritance among the saints,
and what is the surpassing riches of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of the strength of his might,
which he worked in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavens,
far above every rule and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world but also in the one to come.
And he put all things in subjection under his feet, and gave him to the church as head over all things,
which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.
And you were once dead in your trespasses and sins,
in which you once walked according to the ways of this world's age, according to the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit that is now at work among the sons of disobedience,
Among them we all also once lived in the lusts of our flesh, doing the will of our flesh and of our thoughts, and we were by nature children of wrath, just like the others.
But God, because he is great in mercy, through his great love with which he loved us,
even when we were dead in our sins, made us alive together with Christ (by grace you have been saved),
raised us up with him and seated us with him in the heavens through Christ Jesus,
so that in the ages to come he might show the surpassing riches of his grace in kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from you, but it is the gift of God:
not from works, so that no one may boast.
For we are his making, created through Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we should walk in them.
Therefore remember that you were once Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcised by those who are called the circumcision, which is in the flesh and made by hands,
for at that time you were without Christ. You were strangers to the commonwealth of Israel and foreigners to the covenants of the promise. You had no hope, and you were without God in the world.
But now, through Christ Jesus, you who were once far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
For he himself is our peace, who made both into one and broke down the dividing wall of partition,
the enmity, in his flesh. He abolished the law of commandments by a most exalted decree, so that in himself he might create the two into one new man, making peace,
and [?] both of them in one body to God through the cross, having killed the enmity by it,
and he came and proclaimed the good news of peace to you who were far off, and peace to those who were near.
For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.
So from now on you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God.
You are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, whose cornerstone is Christ Jesus,
in whom the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,
in whom you too are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.
For this reason I, Paul, am the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles.
If indeed you have heard of the stewardship of the grace of God that was given to me for you,
for the mystery was made known to me by revelation, as I wrote to you briefly before,
by which you can come to know my understanding of the mystery of Christ,
which was not revealed to the sons of men in other generations as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets by the Holy Spirit,
that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise through Christ Jesus by the gospel,
of which I became a minister according to the gift of the grace of God, given to me by the working of his power.
To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given: to proclaim among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ
and to enlighten everyone about the plan of the mystery that was hidden from the ages with God, who created all things,
so that the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known through the church to the rulers and authorities of heaven,
according to the eternal purpose which he accomplished through Christ Jesus our Lord,
through whom we have boldness and access with hope through faith in him.
Therefore I ask that you not be grieved at my tribulations, which are for your sake and which are your glory.
For this reason I bow my knees to the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man,
so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith,
so that, being established and grounded in love, you may be able to grasp with all the saints what is the breadth and length, the height and depth,
and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him who is able to do far more than all, beyond what we ask or understand, according to the power of his working within us,
to him be glory in the church through Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
I, a prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthily of your calling, the calling to which you have been called,
with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the firm bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called in the one hope of your calling;
one Lord, one faith, and one baptism;
one God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in all.
For grace has been given to each one of us according to the measure of Christ's gift.
Therefore it says: "He ascended on high and led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men."
But what does "he ascended" mean, if not that he first descended to the lower regions of the earth?
He who descended is the same one who ascended above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things.
And he gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, some as shepherds and teachers,
for the strengthening of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,
so that we may no longer be infant children, tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching, by human trickery and by craftiness in the scheming of deception,
but let us be truthful in love and grow up in every way toward him who is the head, Christ,

from whom the whole body is joined together and made firm by every joint of supply, according to the help given in the measure of each member. Bring about the growth of the body, so that you build yourselves up in love.
This I say and testify before the Lord: that you no longer walk as the Gentiles walk, in the futility of their mind.
They are alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, through the blindness of their heart.
They have abandoned themselves and given themselves over to filth, to practise every kind of uncleanness in greed.
But that is not how you learned Christ,
if indeed you have heard him and been taught about him, as the truth is in Jesus.
Put away from yourselves the old man that belongs to your former way of life, which is corrupted by deceitful desires,
and be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
and put on the new man, created by God in righteousness and in the holiness of truth.
Therefore put away falsehood; let each of you speak the truth with his neighbour, for we are members of one another.
Be angry, but do not sin. Do not let the sun go down on your anger.
And do not give the devil a foothold.
Let the thief steal no more. Instead, let him labour and do good with his own hands, so that he may have something to give to anyone in need.
Let no foul word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up where there is need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness and anger, wrath and shouting and slander be removed from you entirely, together with all malice.
Be kind to one another and merciful, forgiving one another, just as God forgave us in Christ.
Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children,
and let us walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us as an offering and a sacrifice to God, a fragrant aroma.
But fornication and every impurity, or covetousness, must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints.
Nor filthiness, foolish talk or levity, which are not fitting; instead, let there be thanksgiving.
But know this: every fornicator, every impure person and every covetous person, who is an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.
So do not become like them,
for you were once darkness, but now you are light through the Lord. As children of light, so let us walk,
for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness and truth.
Test what is pleasing to the Lord,
and take no part in the unfruitful works of darkness; instead, expose them.
For what is done in secret among them is shameful even to speak of.
But everything that is exposed is made manifest by the light, for everything that is made manifest is light.
That is why it says: "Wake up, you who are sleeping, rise from the dead, and Christ will give you light."
So take good care how you walk, not as the foolish but as the wise;
redeem [?] the times, for the days are evil.
Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the will of God is.
And do not get drunk on wine, in which there is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit.
Speak to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs; sing and give praise to God in your heart.
Always give thanks for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Submit to one another in the fear of Christ.
Wives, submit to your own husbands, as to the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the churches, and he himself is the Savior of the body.
But just as the church is subject to Christ, so also wives should be subject to their own husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for it,
so that he might make it holy and cleanse it by the washing of water and by the word,
so that he himself might present the church to himself in glory, having no spot, no wrinkle [?] or any other such thing, but so that it might be holy and blameless.
In the same way husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies, for whoever loves his own wife loves himself.
For no one hates his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ does the Church,
for we are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones.
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife, and the two of them shall be one flesh.
This mystery is great; but I speak concerning Christ and the churches.
But you also, each one of you, love his own wife in this way, as himself; and let the wife fear her husband.
Children, be obedient to your fathers and mothers in the Lord, for this is right.
Honour your father and your mother, which is the first commandment with a promise,
that it may be well with you, and that you may live long on the earth.
And you fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the instruction and teaching of the Lord.
Slaves, be obedient to your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in sincerity of your heart, as to Christ,
and not only before their eyes, with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;
serve with good will, as to the Lord, and not as to man;
knowing that whatever good or evil each one does, that he will also receive from the Lord, whether he is slave or free.
And you masters, do the same toward them, giving up threatening, knowing that their Lord and yours is in heaven, and there is no partiality with him.
Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the might of his strength;
put on the full armour of God, so that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil,

for our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against the principalities and against the powers, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness which are under heaven.
Therefore take up the full armour of God, so that you may be able to withstand in that evil day, and having done everything, to stand firm.
Stand firm, then, having girded your loins with truth, having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
and having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace.
Above all, take up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the wicked one;
and put on the helmet of salvation, and take the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
With all prayer and supplication pray at all times in the Spirit, and keep watch for this with all diligence and supplication for all the saints,
and for me also, that utterance may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make known to you boldly the mystery of the gospel,
for whose sake I am an envoy in chains, so that in it I may speak openly, as it is fitting for me to speak.
So that you too may know about me and what I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you everything.
I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you may know about us and so that he may comfort your hearts.
Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and Jesus our Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption. Amen.
